title: Publisher Correction: A circumbinary protoplanetary disk in a polar configuration
question: What is the orientation, size and structure of the circumbinary disc around HD 98800BaBb, and is it a misaligned, polar, planet-forming disc?

data.sensitivity: rms 14 uJy/beam (Briggs continuum); 0.8 mJy/beam per channel for CO

what.value: BaBb orbit (e=0.785, node 289, i=67 deg) and mass 1.28 Msun

evidence.quote: The binary BaBb is well characterized, with an eccentricity of $0.785 \pm 0.005$

what.value: AB astrometry from the Washington Double Star catalogue

evidence.quote: we obtained previous observations of the AB separation and position angle from the Washington Double Star catalogue (WDS)

what.value: Dust temperature of 160 K from multiwavelength photometry

evidence.quote: assuming a dust temperature of 160K derived from photometry over a range of wavelengths (cite: 1993ApJ...406L..25Z)

recipe.method: Pipeline calibration, one cycle of phase self-cal, concatenate two blocks

recipe.goal: Fit continuum and CO visibilities with a power-law disc model
recipe.method: Line-of-sight integration disc model fit in visibility plane; ring with r_in, r_out, power law, eccentric inner edge for continuum
key_parameters: 64 walkers, 1000 steps after 1000 step burn-in; scale height 0.05r; 2048 pixels of 4.6 mas
assumptions: CO orbits a point mass of 1.28 Msun

recipe.goal: Estimate dust and CO gas masses
recipe.method: Optically thin dust mass from flux; CO mass assuming tau=1, Tex=70 K, H2/CO=1e4
MCMC orbit fit to WDS astrometry plus two radial velocity constraints
assumptions: Mass of A 1.3±0.15 Msun prior; B 1.28 Msun

recipe.method: Gas-free n-body (1 Myr) and SPH simulations of both inclination solutions
Monte Carlo of 1e6 random orientations at 16 eccentricities, separatrix c=e^2
assumptions: Uniform initial orientations, uniform e in 0-0.8

evidence.quote: the inner edges of the dust and CO are at $2.5 \pm 0.02$ and $1.6 \pm 0.3$ au respectively, while the outer edges are at $4.6 \pm 0.01$ and $6.4 \pm 0.5$ au
the inner edges of the dust and CO are at $2.5 \pm 0.02$ and $1.6 \pm 0.3$ au respectively, while the outer edges are at $4.6 \pm 0.01$ and $6.4 \pm 0.5$ au
the disc has a position angle of $16 \pm 1^\circ$ (measured anti-clockwise from North)
Including an absolute calibration uncertainty of 10% yields a final flux measurement of $47 \pm 5$ mJy.
then the total gas mass is roughly 0.28$M_\oplus$
which has an eccentricity of $0.52 \pm 0.01$ and a period of $246 \pm 5$ years

answer_key.quantity: Fraction of discs evolving to polar

not_stated_but_needed: Exact CLEAN parameters (cell, image size, masks, niter, threshold)
Self-cal reference antenna and per-block solint
Prior ranges for MCMC model parameters
Phantom viscosity, disc mass and radii setup
Flux of AA/Ab and AaAb orbit parameters used in n-body
score_reason: Public data, code on github, and most modelling settings stated; some imaging and SPH details missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, a clear visibility-modelling recipe and numeric edges, angles and fluxes.
